name: Ursodeoxycholic acid
route_note: Oral tablets, capsules or suspension, once to several times daily depending on indication

discovery.note: Crystallised from the bile of the Japanese black bear, long used in traditional medicine; later synthesised from cholic acid.

tagline: Bear-bile acid used to dissolve gallstones and treat primary biliary cholangitis
summary: Ursodeoxycholic acid is a hydrophilic secondary bile acid originally found in bear bile. It dissolves cholesterol gallstones in selected patients and is first-line therapy for primary biliary cholangitis, where it improves liver tests and transplant-free survival.
mechanism: UDCA reduces cholesterol secretion into bile and intestinal cholesterol absorption, making bile less saturated and allowing gradual dissolution of cholesterol stones.

In cholestatic liver disease it replaces more toxic hydrophobic bile acids in the bile acid pool, stimulates bile flow and bicarbonate secretion from cholangiocytes, and protects liver cells from bile-acid-induced apoptosis.
uses: Prevention of gallstones during rapid weight loss
Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy and other cholestatic conditions (off-label in some countries)

history.title: Isolation
history.detail: Shoda crystallises ursodeoxycholic acid from black bear bile.

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Japanese chemists report a chemical synthesis, enabling production without bear bile.

history.title: Japanese launch
history.detail: Tokyo Tanabe markets UDCA (Urso) in Japan.

history.title: US approval for gallstones
history.detail: FDA approves Actigall for dissolving gallstones.

history.title: Primary biliary cirrhosis
history.detail: FDA approves Urso for primary biliary cirrhosis (now cholangitis).

history.title: Pregnancy cholestasis trial
history.detail: The PITCHES trial finds UDCA does not reduce adverse perinatal outcomes in intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy.

pk.half_life: Biological half-life in bile acid pool ~3.5–5.8 days
pk.metabolism: Hepatic conjugation with glycine and taurine; bacterial 7-dehydroxylation in colon

facts: Ursodeoxycholic acid's name comes from Ursus, the Latin for bear.
It is the 7β-epimer of chenodeoxycholic acid.
